name: FIBRINOGEN
description: Fibrinogen measures clotting factor I levels and evaluates bleeding disorders, thrombosis risk, and acute phase response. This test assesses fibrinogen deficiency and hyperfibrinogenemia.

testdeatils.instrumentation: Beckman Coulter, Roche Cobas, Abbott Architect

literatureReview: Fibrinogen is clotting factor I, converted to fibrin during coagulation. Normal range 200-400 mg/dL. Low levels (<100 mg/dL) indicate hypofibrinogenemia, DIC, liver disease, or congenital deficiency. High levels (>400 mg/dL) suggest inflammation, infection, or increased thrombosis risk. Clauss method measures functional fibrinogen by thrombin clotting. Used in evaluation of bleeding disorders, DIC diagnosis, and cardiovascular risk assessment. Fibrinogen is an acute phase reactant, rising in inflammation. Critical in perioperative bleeding evaluation and monitoring thrombolytic therapy. Results guide cryoprecipitate transfusion in bleeding patients.
